Earlier, India were in a spot of bother on day 1 after losing their top order cheaply. The West Indian fast bowlers bowled with a lot of fire and venom to have the visiting team on the back foot. But when things were looking gloomy, the pair of Ashwin and Saha got together to thread in a record double century partnership. It helped India post a decent first innings total on the board.

It's comeback time for the hosts! West Indies began the afternoon session rejuvenated and the results showed in their bowling. Both the Indian batsmen, Ashwin and Saha scored their centuries but Alzarri Joseph finally got the breakthrough with Saha's wicket. With the 213-run innings broken, the floodgates opened and the batsmen were unable to stay in for long. Debutant Alzarri Joseph and Miguel Cummins finished with 3 wickets apiece while Roston Chase once again was quite handy with his off spinners, claiming a 2-fer.

Welcome to Day 2 at the Darren Sammy Stadium for  a surprisingly even contest. West Indies got off to a good start and dominated the first half of the previous Day, taking five wickets. The hosts' bowlers lured the batsmen out with their lines and lengths earlier on, taking them by surprise with the bounce. Alzarri Joseph, the Test debutant, is off to an amazing start picking up two crucial wickets. Another bowler to pick up a brace was Roston Chase, who has continued to impress with his bowling, picking up two scalps. Jason Holder, too, played a vital role in keeping the Indian batsmen on their toes.

Ajinkya Rahane held down the fort for a bit with a lengthy yet low scoring partnership with Ashwin but Roston Chase struck again and took him out. Wriddhiman Saha came in and supported Ashwin in rallying their side. Together, they have strung a hard fought partnership of 108 runs, with Ashwin reaching 75. They pushed hard towards the end, taking advantage of the new ball and brought the score up to 234/5.

West Indies wasted no time digging into the batsmen, taking out Shikhar Dhawan and the surprise No. 3 batsman, Virat Kohli, in quick and premature succession. India were in a very shaky position but KL Rahul and Ajinkya Rahane brought some semblance of normalcy back for a while, putting up a 58-run partnership but Rahul was dismissed by Chase just after scoring his half-century.

That brings the day to an end and India will be all too glad. West Indies have undoubtedly called the shots today. They started off on a winning note and have continued their strangle hold on the Indian batsmen till day's close. The resolute Ravichandran Ashwin and Wriddhiman Saha have ended the day on a positive note, pumping up the run rate after the arrival of the new ball. Their contribution has helped bring a more even close to the day's play.

India are on the back foot and are battling it out in the middle. They only scored 43 runs in 29 overs. Indian captain, VIRAT KOHLI says they would have batted first anyway. Adds that it looks like a nice surface with even bounce. He wants to put the opposition under pressure. He has made three changes - Rohit Sharma comes in for Pujara, Ravindra Jadeja replaces Mishra and Bhuvneshwar Kumar comes in for Yadav.

West Indies captain, JASON HOLDER says that they did quite well and will look to carry on. He is very happy with the bowlers who were very consistent and looks to take in one step further this time. He has made two changes - Leon Johnson replaces Chandrika and Alzarri Joseph comes in place of Bishoo.

PITCH REPORT - Jeff Dujon inspects the pitch and says that some of the grass is still green and there is still moisture. He says that it tends to flatten out and will have life early on. Later, it will be really good for the batsmen in the 2nd and 3rd day. Not a lot of crowd is expected but he thinks there will be a lot of action.

The pitch at The Darren Sammy Stadium looks to be on the quicker side and will be friendly to the batsmen and pacers. After the fighting performance that the Windies put up, Indian captain Virat Kohli will have some changes to mull over. Meanwhile, the Men from the Caribbean will be high on confidence after exceeding expectations in the last Test. Stay tuned shortly for the toss!

Hello and welcome to Day 1 of the 3rd Test between West Indies and India at St. Lucia. The visitors lead the series 1-0 with a commanding performance in the first Test. Surprisingly, Roston Chase pulled off a resolute century to help draw the second Test. The pressure will be on India to secure a win this time around as they face an inexperienced and fragile side.
